question: We serve a patient who has just suffered a traffic accident. She is conscious and when taking the constants she has a systolic blood pressure of 70 mmHg and a heart rate of 45 beats / minute. In addition, the skin of the extremities is hot. What is the most likely cause of the shock?
analysis: The patient presents with hypotension (systolic blood pressure of 70 mmHg) and bradycardia (heart rate of 45 beats per minute), along with warm extremities. These symptoms are characteristic of neurogenic shock, which can occur after a traumatic injury, particularly if there is spinal cord involvement. Neurogenic shock is caused by a loss of sympathetic tone, leading to vasodilation and a decrease in heart rate, resulting in warm skin and low blood pressure.
